**Key observations from the test image:**
- Severely twisted/distorted young emerging leaves/shoot
- Multiple narrow leaves spiraling and wrapping around each other
- Pale/cream/white coloration at the base of the twisted portion
- Contorted, stunted appearance of the growing point area
- Overall morphology showing the classic "twisted top" appearance

**Reasoning:** This symptom pattern — twisted, distorted, and rolled young leaves emerging from the growing point with chlorotic/pale areas — is the hallmark of **Pokkah Boeng** disease in sugarcane, caused by *Fusarium verticillioides*. The disease attacks young leaves as they emerge, causing them to twist and become deformed. This is distinct from:
- Grassy Shoot (multiple thin grass-like tillers)
- Mosaic viruses (yellow/green mottling streaks on leaf blade)
- Yellow Leaf (yellowing of midrib on mature leaves)
- Brown Spot / Yellow Spot (discrete spots/lesions on leaf surfaces)
- Leaf Scald (white/cream scalded lesions along margins)
